title.narrative: Djibouti Skills Development for Employment Project

description.narrative: The development objective of the Skills Development for Employment Project for Djibouti is to improve employability and employment outcomes of technical and vocational education and training graduates with a focus on women, persons with disabilities and refugees in priority economic sectors. The project consists of two components. The first component, direct training will support the immediate training needs in the country. It consists of following sub-components: (i) improving employability and employment outcomes through work-based programs; (ii) online acquisition of skills and jobs through scholarships reimbursement and incentive payments; and (iii) developing labor mobility options for Djibouti. The second component, improving technical and vocational education training (TVET) sectoral and institutional governance, architecture and service delivery mechanisms and program management strengthens the existing skills development architecture in Djibouti. It consists of following sub-components: (i) modernizing education and skills governance; (ii) strengthening program quality and relevance; and (iii) project capacity building, management, monitoring and evaluation.

To improve employability and employment outcomes of technical and vocational education and training graduates with a focus on women, persons with disabilities and refugees in priority economic sectors.

condition.narrative: SCHEDULE 2, Section I. A. 2. " In order to ensure proper oversight of the Project and coordination among the Recipient's ministriesinvolved in the Project, the Recipient shall: (a) maintain at all times during the implementation of the Project, the CDE, as asteering committee for the Project, with composition and mandate adequate to carry out the Project and in charge of overalloversight and strategic guidance for the Project (including approval of the Annual Work Plans and Budgets) as further detailed inthe Project Operations Manual; and (b) not later than one (1) month after the Effective Date, execute and thereafter maintain theMemorandum of Understanding detailing the roles and responsibilities of all the Recipient's ministries involved in the Project."

SCHEDULE 2, Section I. A.3. "The Recipient, through MENFOP, shall maintain at all times during Project implementation, the ProjectTechnical Committee (“PTC”) to be in charge of overall Project implementation and coordination, with composition, mandate, staffingand other resources satisfactory to the Association, all in accordance with the provisions of the Project Operations Manual."

SCHEDULE 2, Section I. A.4. "The Recipient, through MENFOP, shall maintain at all times during Project implementation, the ProjectImplementation Unit (“PIU”) to be in charge of overall Project management and monitoring, with composition, mandate, staffing andother resources satisfactory to the Association, all in accordance with the provisions of the Project Operations Manual. To thisend, the Recipient shall no later than one (1) month after the Effective Date, hire and thereafter maintain, throughout Projectimplementation, key staff under the PIU, all with experience and terms of reference, acceptable to the Association, as furtherdetailed in the Project Operations Manual."

SCHEDULE 2, Section I. B. 2. "Work Plans and Budget For purposes of implementation of the Project, the Recipient shall: (a) by nolater than one (1) month after the Effective Date, prepare a draft work plan and budget for Project implementation, setting forth,inter alia: (i) a detailed description of the planned activities, including any proposed Operating Costs and Training, under theProject for the period covered by the plan; (ii) the sources and proposed use of funds therefor; (iii) procurement andenvironmental and social safeguards arrangements therefor, as applicable and; (iv) responsibility for the execution of said Projectactivities, budgets, start and completion dates, outputs and monitoring indicators to track progress of each activity; (...)"

SCHEDULE 2, Section I.C.7. "Without limitation upon the provisions of paragraph 2 above, if 60 days prior to the Closing Date, theAssociation determines that there are measures and actions specified in the ESCP which will not be completed by the Closing Date,the Recipient shall, through MENFOP : (a) not later than 30 days before the Closing Date, prepare and present to the Association,an action plan satisfactory to the Association on the outstanding measures and actions, including a timetable and budget allocationfor such measures and actions (which action plan shall be deemed to be considered an amendment of the ESCP); and (b) thereafter,carry out said action plan in accordance with its terms and in a manner acceptable to the Association."

title.narrative: PDO#3- Share of trainees from project-supported training programs who secure employment in related sectors, disaggregated by gender, disability, and refugee status

title.narrative: PDO#2- Share of girls/women and persons with disabilities completing TVET programs increased

comment.narrative:
This indicator measures the percentage of female students and students with disabilities who completed the program, relative to the total number of students who completed it. Completion is defined as fulfilling all academic and practical requirements established by the training institutions.
The refugee disaggregation, initially considered, will be dropped because refugees in Djibouti primarily pursue general secondary or tertiary education rather than TVET. In addition, most TVET courses are not offered in English, which makes participation by refugees challenging and the category less relevant or representative for data collection purposes.

title.narrative: IRI # 1: Number of trainees engaged in Apprenticeships, Internships, OJT, and Entrepreneurship programs (disaggregated by gender, disability and refugee status)

comment.narrative: Several training courses are currently being finalized based on market needs, and the Department of Labor has launched the third cohort for field prospecting as part of the internship program.

title.narrative: IRI # 1: Number of trainees engaged in Apprenticeships, Internships, OJT, and Entrepreneurship programs (disaggregated by gender, disability and refugee status)

comment.narrative: To date, 149 participants have been placed in apprenticeships, internships, and on-the-job training programs. The final target will be revised to 1000 participants (500 girls, 80 persons with disabilities, and 100 refugees) to reflect (i) high unit training and placement costs, (ii) limited labor market absorption capacity, and (iii) operational delays linked to the procedures manual and new sectoral partnerships. In addition, refugee relocation to provinces and the phase-out of UNHCR camp support constrained placement opportunities. The revised target is therefore more realistic given current market and institutional conditions.

title.narrative: IRI # 2: Number of learners certified from online training (disaggregated by gender, disability and refugee status)

comment.narrative: Several online training courses have been launched in English, covering topics such as Windows Office, procurement, monitoring and evaluation, cybersecurity, etc.

title.narrative: IRI # 2: Number of learners certified from online training (disaggregated by gender, disability and refugee status)

comment.narrative: To date, 461 have completed qualifications online, of which 199 female, 33 persons with disabilities and 8 refugees. The indicator will be revised from “Number of trainees reimbursed after completing their online qualifications (disaggregated by gender, refugee status, and persons with disabilities)” to “Number of learners certified online (disaggregated by gender, refugee status, and persons with disabilities),” and the final target increased from 500 to 1,000. This change reflects both the stronger-than-expected demand and results achieved to date, as well as the need to shift the focus from the reimbursement mechanism, which was more process-oriented, to certification outcomes, which more accurately capture the project's impact on skills acquisition and learner achievement.

comment.narrative: This indicator measures the cumulative number of students newly enrolled in selected TVET programs, disaggregated by gender and disability status. comment.narrative: This indicator will be deleted during the upcoming restructuring. The reason for removing this indicator is as follows: it relates to the initial training of trainers, which would require the ministry to recruit an additional 250 trainers to reach the final target of 720, knowing that 470 have already been trained. However, given the decision to reduce the number of constructions, MENFOP will no longer recruit as many trainers as planned.

title.narrative: IRI #13: Communication campaign to promote youth participation in project activities.

comment.narrative: This new indicator will measure the extent to which the project undertakes formal communication efforts to raise awareness, enhance visibility, and encourage active engagement of young people in project-supported activities. A “communication campaign” is defined as a coordinated set of outreach actions (e.g., social media, radio, community events, posters, workshops) implemented within a defined timeframe, with clear messaging, target audience, and measurable outputs.

title.narrative: IRI #13: Communication campaign to promote youth participation in project activities.

comment.narrative: A communications agency has been hired, and the Department of Education and the Department of Labor have already approved the communications strategy. Everyone involved in the project has been able to develop their own communications plan and prioritize activities.
